brief_title: Achieving Normal Glucose In Hospital Settings
official_title: An Open-label, Single-centre, Randomised, Two-period Crossover Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of 24-hour Closed-loop Glucose Control in Comparison With Conventional Treatment in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes on Non-insulin Glucose-lowering Agents
collaborators: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

primary_outcomes.measure: Percent of plasma glucose values within target range 3.9-8.0 mmol/l

brief_summary: The main objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 24 hours of closed-loop glucose control compared with standard diabetes treatment, in patients with type 2 diabetes treated by non-insulin glucose-lowering medications. This group is being studied as it is representative of patients with glucose dysregulation.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 18 years or older
* Type 2 diabetes for at least 1 year as defined by WHO
* Treatment with glucose-lowering medication(s) (including Exenatide) for at least 6 mths
* HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.0% inclusive (measured within past 3 mths)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Autoimmune type 1 diabetes
* Type 2 diabetes treated with insulin
* Type 2 diabetes treated with diet control alone
* Known or suspected allergy against insulin
* Proliferative retinopathy
* Current or planned pregnancy or breast feeding
* Any physical or psychological disease or medication(s) likely to interfere with the conduct of the study and interpretation of the study results, as judged by the study clinician
